samples.summary: Remote `listLevel` from a peer's Yorkie tree attribute is still ingested with a bare `Number(...)` and no clamp; the new module normalizes only on the planning path, leaving every geometry sink reading the raw value
samples.evidence: `treeNodeToBlock` does `block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)` (crdt-tree.ts:243) with no finiteness or range check, so a malicious/compromised collaborator (or a crafted revision/DOCX/API payload) can publish `listLevel: "1e309"` or `"NaN"`. The new `levelOf()` in packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:30-33 clamps only when an indent/outdent gesture happens to touch the block; the read paths keep multiplying the raw value into geometry: layout.ts:494 `LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)`, table-layout.ts:93, paint-layout.ts:198, doc-canvas.ts:599, peer-cursor.ts:254/392 and export/pdf-painter.ts:366 — the new code's own comment at list-level.ts:100-101 acknowledges "the layout pass, which reads `listLevel` raw". Effect on every peer rendering the doc is NaN/Infinity marginLeft and effectiveWidth, i.e. corrupted or blank layout and caret geometry pushed off-canvas. I traced the taint from ingest to the multiplication sinks but could NOT confirm a hard hang: the char-wrap fallback in layout.ts:764-794 always advances `charIdx`, so NaN comparisons degrade to one over-long line rather than an infinite loop. Also note the write side is only safe by accident: MAX_LIST_LEVEL is enforced in the clipboard sanitizer (clipboard.ts:348-351) and in the planner, but nothing enforces it on `setBlockType`/store writes generally. Since a poisoning peer needs edit rights (read-only mounts are neutered by store/read-only.ts), this is hardening rather than privilege escalation — but the clamp belongs at the ingest boundary the new MAX_LIST_LEVEL constant now centralizes.
searchedFor: Grep 'ilvl' repo-wide for XML export sinks

samples.summary: The new `applyListLevelChanges` in the docs text-box editor (mounted by Slides/Board) writes to blocks the selection never covered, and this editor has no read-only/permission concept at all
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts` contains no `readOnly` gate (grep for `readOnly` in that file returns nothing), and neither does the Slides wrapper `packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts`. The docs full editor closes this hole two ways — `readOnlyDocStore` (store/read-only.ts:67) and the `MUTATING_METHODS` neutering that includes `indent`/`outdent` (view/editor.ts:4492) — but the text-box API's `indent()`/`outdent()` (text-box-editor.ts:1164, 1183) reach `doc.setBlockType` directly, now for carried children outside the selection too. I could not find a viewer-reachable mount of this API, so the gating may simply live at the Slides/Board mount decision; reported for completeness because the diff widens what one call to this ungated surface writes.

searchedFor: grep listLevel across packages/docs, packages/frontend, packages/backend, packages/slides
finding.summary: Peer-supplied `listLevel` is still read through a bare `Number(...)` with no clamp; the new `levelOf()` normalizer only protects the planner, so a poisoned level keeps reaching raw sinks (unbounded `String.repeat` in the markdown serializer, NaN/huge geometry in layout and PDF)
finding.evidence: The new module documents the threat itself (`packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:19-27`: "a peer's Tree attribute is read straight through `Number(...)`") and claims "Normalizing at the single point of read is what keeps both guards total". That is only true inside `planListLevelChanges`. The actual read boundaries are unchanged and unclamped: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495` (`block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)`) and `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243` (same line, used for revision previews). Attack: a principal with write access to a shared doc (collaborator, or an API key with write scope via `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/content`, which does not validate `listLevel` — see the companion finding) stores `listLevel: 1e9` (or `1e400` → `"Infinity"`). Every other reader then deserializes it verbatim. Sinks reached with the raw value: `packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:140` `'  '.repeat(Math.max(0, block.listLevel ?? 0))` → 2e9-char allocation or `RangeError: Invalid string length`, crashing `wafflebase docs content get --format md` (`packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129`) for anyone who exports the document; `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:494` `LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` → NaN/Infinity `marginLeft` that collapses or blanks the rendered document; `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:377` → NaN/huge coordinates into pdf-lib. Note the adjacent `headingLevel` is clamped at its sink (`markdown.ts:156 clampHeadingLevel`) while `listLevel` is not. This is a persistent, other-user-affecting availability/data-integrity issue, not merely a local render glitch.

verdict.reason: All claimed code is present as described. `levelOf()` in packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:29-33 is module-private and used only by the planner (lines 50, 56, 92, 102) — it is not exported and does not run at either deserialization boundary. Both read boundaries remain bare and unclamped: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495 and packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243 both do `Number(attrs.listLevel)`, so NaN/Infinity/1e9 survive. The raw value then reaches unbounded sinks: markdown.ts:140 `'  '.repeat(Math.max(0, block.listLevel ?? 0))` (Math.max only blocks negatives, not huge values -> multi-GB allocation or RangeError), layout.ts:494, and pdf-painter.ts:366/377 (NaN/huge PDF coordinates). The asymmetry the reviewer notes is real: the adjacent heading case clamps at markdown.ts:132 via clampHeadingLevel (markdown.ts:156-160) while list-item does not. No upstream guard exists on the write path: packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178 stringifies listLevel verbatim with no validation, and the only clamp in the tree (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:348-349) is on the clipboard-paste path, which peer/API writes bypass. The markdown sink is reachable via CLI export (packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:119,124). This is untrusted, persistently-stored input reaching a resource-exhaustion/geometry sink affecting other users — unsafe input handling in the security lane, not a correctness-only nit. No named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: The docs content PUT validator checks every block-style numeric is finite but never validates `listLevel`, so the API is an unvalidated injection point for the out-of-range/non-finite list levels the new planner's normalizer exists to defend against
finding.evidence: `assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:429-511) validates `id`, `type`, `style` shape, `style.alignment` against an allowlist and every `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` entry as a finite number (:399-407), and `assertValidHeaderFooter` even validates `marginFromEdge` as finite (:331-339) — but nothing checks `listLevel`. `buildBlockNode` then persists it verbatim: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178` `attrs.listLevel = String(block.listLevel)`. So `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/content` with `{blocks:[{id:"a",type:"list-item",listLevel:1e9,inlines:[],style:{}}]}` is accepted by an authenticated write-scoped caller and lands in the CRDT for every collaborator, where the readers cited in the companion finding consume it raw (`'  '.repeat(1e9)` in the markdown serializer → RangeError/GB allocation; NaN geometry in layout). The clamp exists in exactly two places today — the clipboard parser and the new `levelOf` in `model/list-level.ts:29-33` — and neither is on this path. `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` is now an exported model constant, so the same bound is trivially applicable here (`@wafflebase/docs` is already imported by this controller at :44-49).

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. I read docs-content.controller.ts in full: assertValidBlock (:429-512) and assertValidBlockStyle (:380-427) validate id/type/style/alignment, every BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS entry as finite (:399-407), AUTHORED_SPACING_FIELDS as boolean (:418-426), and assertValidHeaderFooter validates marginFromEdge as finite (:331-339) — but no branch anywhere in the docs or slides arms inspects listLevel (or headingLevel). No other guard covers the path: @Body() is typed `unknown` (:158) so the global ValidationPipe (packages/backend/src/main.ts:65-66) has no metatype to validate against, and the writer persists the value verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178 `attrs.listLevel = String(block.listLevel)`). A repo-wide grep for MAX_LIST_LEVEL/clampListLevel/normalizeListLevel/levelOf finds only two clamps — packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:351 (paste parser) and packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:29-33 (planner-only levelOf) — neither on this request path, and the CRDT reader re-hydrates raw (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243 `Number(attrs.listLevel)`, so a string body value becomes NaN). Downstream readers consume it unguarded: packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:140 `'  '.repeat(...)` and packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:1089-1092 `levelCounters.length = Math.max(len, level + 1)` (RangeError: Invalid array length for NaN). Net effect: an authenticated write-scoped caller stores a poisoned listLevel that crashes/hangs every other collaborator's client — unsafe input handling reaching a persistent shared sink, within the security lane. Found no counterexample.
